transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), Jonas (Platform), Lena (Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/deck/nyx-integration, drive:nyx-security-whitepaper-link

Summary: quick discovery focused on integration approach (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), gateway/proxy patterns, SDK compatibility (LangChain/LlamaIndex), rate limits & quotas, and observability hooks. Customer concerned about PII workloads, on-prem options, and traffic shaping for bursty API usage.

Topics: integration patterns, VPC onramp, sidecar gateway vs central proxy, per-route quotas, batching/kv cache, observability/tracing, pilot metrics.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for taking time, uh we'll do a quick intro and then dive into how you might integrate Redwood with your stack
[00:12] Priya: thanks Maya, yeah we are short on time, main goals are: low latency for user-facing features, keep costs predictable, and make sure sensitive customer data never leaks out of our environment
[00:22] Ravi: mm-hmm, totally. quick question on your current infra — are you running models in-house now or using any hosted APIs?
[00:30] Jonas: right now it's a hybrid; we have an internal inference cluster for a small set of models, but most prototyping uses MegaCloudAI. we want to standardize on something that can scale and give us controls for production
[00:41] Lena: and from security, we need KMS integration, audit logs, and the ability to run in a private VPC or on-premise for regulated tenants
[00:50] Maya: great — that's why we wanted to cover Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. quick overview: Hosted is fastest to get going (Redwood-managed), Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation, Private is customer-controlled (VPC / on-prem) with KMS/HSM support and audit logs
[01:05] Priya: can you explain how the onramp works for Private? we have strict egress rules and need to keep everything behind our transit gateway
[01:13] Ravi: yeah absolutely; for Private we provide a customer-managed control plane — you deploy a lightweight onramp connector that creates an encrypted tunnel into your VPC or an air-gapped package for on-prem. the onramp can be deployed as a helm chart or as a VM image. traffic stays in your network and you can route logs to your observability stack
[01:30] Jonas: so is that sidecar vs central proxy? what's recommended for teams that run multiple services calling LLMs?
[01:38] Ravi: two patterns: 1) sidecar pattern — sidecar per service for low-latency local calls and local caching (good for microservices), 2) central gateway/proxy — a single edge proxy that handles routing, rate limiting, auth, and batching. if you have many small services, sidecar gives the best latency; central proxy simplifies policy and quota enforcement
[01:55] Priya: what's the effort to adopt LangChain and LlamaIndex? those are core to our app layer
[02:03] Maya: we have first-class SDKs for Python and Node, and maintained connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Ravi: we also provide an example LangChain agent that wires to our streaming endpoint and handles function calls and tool orchestration
[02:18] Jonas: sweet. how do you handle embeddings — do we need to host an embedding model or can we use Redwood-hosted embeddings with private data?
[02:26] Ravi: Hosted embeddings are available; for Private we can deploy embedding models in your VPC and you control the data. we also support hybrid flows — embeddings generated in your VPC but stored in your vector DB of choice
[02:37] Lena: compliance question — do you support customer KMS for key wrapping and do you provide exportable audit logs?
[02:44] Maya: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integration and we export structured audit logs. we'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 report after the call
[02:55] Priya: rate limits & quotas — we have bursty traffic on signup flows. can you do per-route and per-tenant quotas?
[03:03] Ravi: yes, we provide per-API-key, per-route, and per-tenant quotas. token-based rate limiting is configurable with token-bucket policies and we support different priority lanes (low cost batch lane vs low-latency lane). you can also set dynamic routing rules — e.g., send to Dedicated for SLA-critical flows, fallback to Hosted for overflow
[03:23] Jonas: curious about batching — we want to avoid queues causing latency spikes; how does Redwood do continuous batching without increasing p95 too much?
[03:31] Ravi: our runtime does workload-aware batching with latency SLOs — it will batch opportunistically but enforce a hard latency cutoff so tokens flush if the batch isn't filled. there's also prefix/KV cache so repeated context doesn't need to be recomputed, which reduces end-to-end time for many chat scenarios
[03:49] Priya: on the topic of caching — can we share KV cache across replicas or is it per-instance?
[03:55] Ravi: KV cache is managed per inference node but we support warm start and shared cache layers in Dedicated/Private setups. we can walk through cache sizing in the pilot
[04:07] Lena: observability — we use Datadog & Splunk. we need per-request traces, token breakdowns, and cost attribution back to a product owner.
[04:16] Maya: Console exposes per-route token/cost breakdowns, p50/p95 latency, and trace ids. we can deliver logs through a push integration or forward them to your SIEM. Ravi: plus we've got SDK-level hooks for attaching request metadata and OpenTelemetry spans
[04:30] Jonas: good, we want to link traces back to our request ids and put alerts on regression in output quality
[04:35] Ravi: you can push evaluation alerts tied to prompt sets — Redwood Optimize can surface regressions and tie them to model/version/rollouts
[04:45] Maya: regarding deployment and rollouts, you can pin model versions, run canaries, and define fallback policies so if the main model fails we go to a smaller/lightweight variant
[04:56] Priya: what about local debugging — can devs point SDKs at a local mock or the Dedicated cluster?
[05:02] Ravi: yes, SDKs support env overrides — devs can run a local stub or point to a staging Dedicated endpoint, same API surface as Hosted
[05:11] Jonas: on cost — any knobs besides batching and quantization? we have long context requests sometimes
[05:18] Ravi: quantization profiles, shorter context windows, caching, and routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical traffic. Redwood Optimize can recommend settings per workload to meet cost/latency targets
[05:31] Lena: network egress is a concern on Hosted — how do you guarantee data residency?
[05:36] Maya: Hosted stores data in specific cloud regions; for regulated tenants we recommend Dedicated or Private so data never leaves your VPC. we'll include region and data residency docs
[05:47] Priya: Pilots — we want to run a two-week pilot that includes a real traffic replay for signup flows and chat. what metrics should we capture?
[05:56] Ravi: capture p50/p95 latency, token throughput, error rates, model output diffs, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll provide a benchmarking harness — we usually measure 95th end-to-end and headroom under concurrency
[06:12] Jonas: for traffic replay, can we run against a Dedicated pool with small reserved capacity?
[06:16] Maya: yes, we can provision a small Dedicated pool for the pilot. that gets you predictable latency and allows measuring scaling behavior
[06:24] Priya: security: do you allow us to bring our own certs for TLS termination on the onramp?
[06:30] Ravi: yes, BYO certs are supported; you control TLS termination in the Private deployment
[06:35] Priya: any gotchas with LlamaIndex? we've had issues with vector store auth in other setups
[06:42] Ravi: our connector includes auth helpers for common vector stores and examples for secure credential management. if you use a proprietary vector store we'll pair up to build the adapter during the pilot
[06:52] Jonas: requests per second — can we throttle at the gateway so we don't overwhelm backends during spikes?
[06:57] Ravi: absolutely, gateway supports rate limiting both at request and token levels plus burst windows. you can configure backpressure policies to return 429 or queue short-lived bursts
[07:07] Lena: auditability — we need tamper-evident logs for compliance; is there a way to ship signed logs?
[07:13] Maya: we can provide signed append-only logs for Private customers and integrate with your archival process. we'll include a sample setup in the security packet
[07:23] Priya: do you have multi-tenant isolation guarantees for Dedicated? some tenants are subject to stricter SLAs
[07:30] Ravi: Dedicated is single-tenant GPU pools per customer, but you can still have logical workspaces inside. for strict isolation we recommend Private where compute sits in your environment
[07:40] Jonas: latency targets — what p95 for a 4k context generation on a Dedicated A100 pool?
[07:46] Ravi: typical p95 for 4k on Dedicated optimized runtime is in the 200-400ms per token ballpark depending on model; end-to-end will vary with decoding settings. we'll run a benchmark with your prompts to be precise
[07:58] Priya: that's promising, but we need the numbers under our real payloads
[08:03] Maya: agreed — that's why pilot benchmarks are important. we'll instrument with your requests and report back
[08:10] Jonas: instrumenting — will you push traces to our Datadog?
[08:14] Ravi: yes, OpenTelemetry spans and metrics can be exported to Datadog. we also have sample dashboards you can import
[08:21] Priya: about SDKs — how stable are the LangChain connectors and do they support streaming responses and function calling?
[08:28] Ravi: connectors support streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output parsing. we maintain compatibility with LangChain releases and have CI tests for those connectors
[08:38] Lena: any special network requirements for the onramp? egress ports or NAT?
[08:43] Ravi: minimal egress for control plane during deployment, everything else is over TLS. for air-gapped on-prem we provide an offline installer. we'll send the firewall requirements doc
[08:53] Jonas: failure modes — if a model explodes under load, can traffic be rerouted automatically?
[08:58] Maya: yes, you can set automated fallbacks and rate-based circuit breakers. Redwood Console can orchestrate canaries and auto-failover to smaller model variants or alternate regions
[09:10] Priya: legal/procurement — what's your standard SLA and lead time to provision Dedicated?
[09:16] Maya: Dedicated SLA options vary; typical lead time to spin a small Dedicated pool is 1-2 weeks after contract, depending on region. we'll include standard SLA language in the pricing packet
[09:26] Jonas: integration effort estimate — for our platform team, how many days to integrate SDK + gateway?
[09:31] Ravi: for a central gateway plus LangChain connectors expect ~2-3 engineering days to wire in core flows, plus 1 week to harden quotas and observability. sidecar pattern adds a bit more per-service
[09:45] Priya: can you share an example Terraform for the VPC onramp?
[09:48] Ravi: yes, I'll share a repo with Terraform and Helm examples after the call
[09:52] Maya: ok i'm going to summarize next steps and then open the floor for anything else
[09:56] Maya: next steps: send pricing/SLA/security docs, Ravi to provision test repo, schedule pilot kickoff. any other open questions?
[10:06] Lena: one more — do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for Console?
[10:10] Ravi: yes SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported. for Private we can sync with your identity provider
[10:16] Priya: thanks all, this was useful. we'll review docs and confirm pilot stakeholders
[10:21] Maya: perfect, talk soon

End notes: occasional transcription glitches (names and acronyms sometimes misrecognized). references: security whitepaper (drive link), example Terraform repo (github.com/redwood/nyx-onramp-sample), benchmark harness (internal link).
